name: file-company-tax-return-with-accounts
title: File the accounts and the Company Tax Return together
description: A signed-in walk through filing a company's annual accounts at Companies House and its Company Tax Return at HMRC as one filing: sign in, take out Resident Ltd, look up a company, drop the book, choose to send to both, review what each receives, file, and see both receipts under one filing.

steps.caption: A sandbox preview against HMRC's test service.
steps.headline: A sandbox preview

steps.text: See the full sign-in walkthrough in our sign-in video.
steps.headline: Sign in, faster

steps.caption: Sign in with the account you already use.
steps.headline: Sign in first

steps.caption: Your account keeps your filings in one place.
steps.headline: Confirm your identity

steps.caption: Bundles decide which activities you can run.
steps.headline: Open your bundles

steps.caption: Resident Ltd opens the Company Tax Return filing.
steps.headline: Unlock the tax return

steps.caption: Every activity starts from the home page.
steps.headline: Go to activities

steps.label: Waiting for the subscription to unlock the activity

steps.caption: Open File Company Tax Return to find the company.
steps.headline: Find the company
steps.instruction: Choose File Company Tax Return (HMRC) on the activities page.

steps.caption: Type the company number.
steps.headline: Enter the company number
steps.instruction: Enter your company number.

steps.caption: Look up the company with Companies House.
steps.headline: Look up the company
steps.instruction: Choose Look up company.

steps.caption: Companies House confirms the company name.
steps.headline: Confirm the company name
steps.instruction: Check that the company name Companies House shows is the company you mean.

steps.caption: Drop the company's diya-gl book on the form.
steps.headline: Drop your book
steps.instruction: Drop the company's diya-gl book on the box that says Drop a book here.

steps.label: Reading the book
steps.caption: The accounts and the tax figures fill from the book.
steps.headline: The form fills itself
steps.instruction: Read the status line that says the accounts and tax figures are filled from the book.

steps.caption: Turnover comes straight from the book.
steps.headline: Turnover from the book
steps.instruction: Check Turnover against your book.

steps.note: A book holds no approval date; the step has no caption so the guide keeps the published video's frames.

steps.caption: The tax is worked out beside your answers.
steps.headline: The tax is worked out
steps.instruction: Read the tax that is worked out beside your answers.

steps.caption: The accounts can go to HMRC alone, or to Companies House and HMRC together.
steps.headline: Choose where they go
steps.instruction: Read the Send to choice: HMRC alone, or Companies House and HMRC together.

steps.caption: Choose to send to Companies House and to HMRC.
steps.headline: Send to both
steps.instruction: Choose Send to Companies House and to HMRC.

steps.caption: Companies House gets the accounts first. HMRC follows when it accepts them.
steps.headline: Companies House first
steps.instruction: Read the hint under the send choice: Companies House gets the accounts first.

steps.caption: Companies House gets the balance sheet and notes. HMRC also gets the profit and loss.
steps.headline: What Companies House gets
steps.instruction: Read the note that lists what each recipient receives.

steps.caption: The director's name comes from the book.
steps.headline: Director from the book
steps.instruction: Check the name of the person signing the declaration against your book.

steps.caption: Type the company's Unique Taxpayer Reference.
steps.headline: Enter the UTR
steps.instruction: Enter the Tax reference.

steps.caption: Accept the four statutory statements.
steps.headline: Accept the statements
steps.instruction: Tick each of the four statements under Statements to accept.

steps.caption: Tick the declaration to confirm the return is accurate.
steps.headline: Confirm the declaration
steps.instruction: Tick the declaration that the return is correct and complete.

steps.caption: Preview the return before anything is sent.
steps.headline: Preview the return
steps.instruction: Choose Preview the return, then read it before anything is sent.

steps.caption: The review says Companies House gets the accounts first, then HMRC.
steps.headline: Companies House first
steps.instruction: Read the review row that says Companies House gets the accounts first.

steps.caption: HMRC receives the full accounts with the return.
steps.headline: What HMRC receives
steps.instruction: Read the review row that lists the accounts HMRC receives.

steps.caption: These are the CT600 boxes as HMRC will receive them.
steps.headline: The CT600 boxes
steps.instruction: Check the CT600 boxes as HMRC will receive them.

steps.caption: The tax computation sits beside the return.
steps.headline: The tax computation
steps.instruction: Read the tax computation under the CT600 boxes.

steps.caption: Type the company's Companies House authentication code.
steps.headline: Enter the auth code
steps.instruction: Enter the Company authentication code that Companies House issued.

steps.caption: Type the company's Government Gateway user ID.
steps.headline: Enter the Gateway user ID
steps.instruction: Enter the Government Gateway user ID.

steps.caption: Type the Government Gateway password.
steps.headline: Enter the password
steps.instruction: Enter the Government Gateway password.

steps.caption: Send the accounts to Companies House, then the return to HMRC.
steps.headline: Send to both
steps.instruction: Choose Submit to HMRC to send the accounts and then the return.

steps.label: Waiting for Companies House
steps.caption: Companies House accepts the accounts first.
steps.headline: Companies House accepts
steps.instruction: Read the Companies House outcome to check it accepted the accounts.

steps.label: Waiting for HMRC
steps.caption: Then HMRC accepts the Company Tax Return.
steps.headline: HMRC accepts the return
steps.instruction: Read the result to check that HMRC accepted the Company Tax Return.

steps.caption: The IRmark proves the return arrived unchanged.
steps.headline: The IRmark
steps.instruction: Read the IRmark in the result and keep it with your record.

steps.caption: Both filings are accepted under one entry.
steps.headline: Both filings accepted
steps.instruction: Read the result that shows both filings as accepted under one entry.

steps.caption: Your receipts page lists the accounts and the return as one filing.
steps.headline: One filing, two receipts
steps.instruction: Choose Receipts to find the accounts and the return listed as one filing.

steps.caption: Open your copy of the Company Tax Return.
steps.headline: Open your copy
steps.instruction: Choose the first receipt to open your copy of the Company Tax Return.

steps.caption: It ends with the status and the date filed.
steps.headline: Status and date filed
steps.instruction: Scroll to the end of the filing to read the status and the date filed.
